bounds.domain: Two callers and two roots. Admission has one active caller, five provider behavior classes, missing/present credentials, five finite expiry positions, seven raw requested-buffer equivalence classes and explicit/missing/stale policy authority. Protocol cases use two callers, one provider class, one external replace/delete/reset, two success lifetimes, optional token rotation and eight provider/transport response classes plus a request deadline. Logical time 0..3, at most five allocated record generations.
bounds.assumptions: RefreshMutex supplies a process-local FIFO queue for the same provider/account key. AccountCredentialGeneration supplies atomic generation CAS, and AccountStorageLock/AccountStorageReset supply the filesystem ownership and epoch fence. These are separate checked contracts. Signature validation, cryptography and remote provider behavior are not proved. No process-global mutex is assumed across processes. Successful one-time rotation marks the used remote grant; malformed/transport responses may have consumed it without a durable local record.
bounds.progress: Weak fairness of call start, FIFO admission, the existing five-second AbortSignal refresh deadline, and storage completion. External provider replies are not required for queue release because the deadline aborts header/body I/O. The model abstracts elapsed wall time as a fair deadline action. Atomic API decisions use the observed record and decision time; later consumer delays can expire an issued token.
bounds.limitations: One external mutation and two calls bound the coordination cases. Metadata/id-token merge is covered by AccountCredentialGeneration. Full provider enrollment, pool health transitions, arbitrary retries, process death and durable credential recovery remain separate models. Real conformance covers named HTTP/filesystem/process schedules, not every abstract interleaving.

assumptions: CallsSettle is conditional on FairWork, which gives weak fairness to each caller start, FIFO admission, providerDeadline and commitWork action.
The native five-second AbortSignal request deadline eventually fires and aborts unfinished provider headers or body reads. Provider success or response delivery is not required.

Each admitted storage operation eventually settles by returning a value or throwing. Schedulers, timers, cryptography, arbitrary process death and concrete implementation refinement remain outside the finite proof.
Each bounded caller starts once. The projection contains at most two calls and one external replace, delete or reset operation; it makes no unbounded retry or successful-provider progress claim.
